What kind of games? For most games, the controller is pretty universal, but some games you don't want a console controller for. FPS and RTS are best suited for mouse and keyboard, fighting games are best suited for arcade sticks and rocker dpad only controllers. The rest are pretty much fine on analog controllers.

you wouldn't really want it for that game-set as much as a mouse and keyboard and a typical style controller. but it is usable. it is best used for games like civ5, which are virtually unplayable on an xbox style controller. imagine what would be nice with two laptop track-pads but physical buttons added.

So, I got to play with one of the Steam controllers at PAX Prime and I have to say I was not a fan.

In order to get the touchpad to reliably track finger movement, they had to enlarge it, which led to the XYAB buttons getting shifted to an uncomfortable position. It felt like a mirror image of an XBox 360 controller (the movement stick was pushed down right, the camera stick was pushed up right) with poorer camera manipulation (they had to jack up the auto-aim feature in Borderlands, the game I tested it on, in order to hit anything).

If you're going to game on a PC, I honestly recommend an XBox 1 controller. If you have Windows it just plug and plays without issue. Otherwise, if you don't want the wire, PS4 controllers can use Bluetooth pretty seamlessly.
